title: Small People Under a Vast Sky
overview: A song of wonder that the God who made the huge night sky pays attention to small human beings and gives them honor and a place of responsibility in the world.

parts.label: God's greatness everywhere (vv. 1, 9)
parts.note: The singer praises God's name, meaning God's whole character and reputation, as majestic across the earth and above the skies. The same line opens and closes the song, wrapping everything in between in praise.

parts.label: Strength from small voices (v. 2)
parts.note: This verse is hard to translate, and scholars are unsure of its exact sense. The general idea seems to be that God can use the weakest voices, even young children, to silence those who oppose him.

parts.label: Tiny under the night sky (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: Looking up at the moon and stars, which God shaped as easily as with his fingers, the writer feels how small and fragile humans are. The surprise is that the Maker of all that still keeps people in mind and cares for them.

parts.label: Crowned with honor (v. 5)
parts.note: People are made just a little lower than God, or than the angels; the Hebrew word can mean either, so translations differ. They are crowned with glory and honor, words usually used of kings.

parts.label: In charge of creation (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Humans are given charge over flocks, wild animals, birds and fish, echoing the creation story in Genesis 1. Christians, following the New Testament letter to the Hebrews, read these lines as finding their full meaning in Jesus.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether verses 4 to 8 are mainly about humanity's place in the world in general or mainly a prophecy that is truly fulfilled only in Jesus.
think: When you look up at a night sky, do you feel small, significant, or both, and what do you make of that feeling?
